texts.preamble: M/S.Jaiswal Products vs The Tamilnadu State on 18 August, 2022 Author: N.Sathish Kumar Bench: N.Sathish Kumar Crl.O.P.No In The High Court Of Judicature At Madras Dated : 18.08.2022 Coram: The Hon'Ble Mr.Justice N.Sathish Kumar
texts.facts: ORDER This Criminal Original Petition is filed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., to call for the records and quash the charge sheet in S.T.C.No.624 of 2019, for the offence under Section 3(1)(zz)(i)(iii)(v) of FSS Act, 2006 and Rules 2, 3, 4 of the Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and restrictions of sales) Regulations Ac, 2011, pending on the file of Judicial Magistrate-I, Attur, Salem. 2.It is the case of the prosecution that on 07.03.2018, when the complainant conducted inspection in the food shop at Vasatham Coffee Bar, Attur Block, Kothamwadi, Salem, he found the tobacco product known as Hans Chhap Tobacco and seized the product. The Food Safety Officer collected the sample and sent the same to the Laboratory for analysis. On analysis, it was found that the sample falls under the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis category of Panmasala and contains Nicotain to an extent of 1.7%, which is injuries to health resulting in the launching of the prosecution against the seller and the petitioner herein, who is the manufacturer.
texts.arguments: 3.The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner contended that the prosecution launched as against the petitioner is without any basis. In fact, Tobacco is not a food product and permission has been granted to sell such product in two States in India, namely Karnataka and Delhi and when the writ petitions were filed before the Delhi Court, the Delhi High Court also directed the respondent not to take any coercive action against the petitioner and the petitioner is manufacturing the product only after obtaining permission in the above States and he is no way connected with the sale of the products in Tamil Nadu. It is his further contention that the petitioner herein never involved in such sale in Tamil Nadu and the referral lab report also clearly indicates that the Tobacco is not a food product and it falls only under the category of tobacco products. The learned counsel contended that without any materials to show that the manufacturer is involved in selling the products in Tamil Nadu, https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis mechanically the prosecution has been launched against the petitioner. 4.Learned Additional Public Prosecutor submitted that the report of the Food Analyst clearly shows that the tobacco falls under the category of Panmasala and the sample contains Nicotin which is unsafe to use. It is his further contention that when the petitioner himself has admitted that he is the manufacturer, he is also liable to be prosecuted and opposed for quashing of the proceedings. 5. Normally, this Court would be reluctant to interfere with the complaint, but at the same time when the materials relied upon by the prosecution, in the considered view of the Court, do not M/S.Jaiswal Products vs The Tamilnadu State on 18 August, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175183719/ 2 constitute any offence against the person and continuation of the prosecution is a sheer waste of time and futile exercise, this Court can very well exercise its power under Section 482 Cr.P.C. Therefore, in the absence of any nexus between sale and supply by the manufacturer and when the m a n u f a c t u r i n g o f t h e p r o d u c t i s p e r m i t t e d i n n e i g h b o u r i n g S t a t e s , t h e https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
